A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same phase-transition study. Their complete main texts, figures, equations, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison despite changes in title, numbering, and layout.

before.justification: v1 reports original Poisson simulations in Section 4 and Figure 2, measuring M-estimator existence across dimension ratios and signal strengths using 20 repetitions.

after.justification: v3 reports Poisson simulations and additional binary/binomial simulations in Section 4 and Figures 2–3, with empirical frequencies of M-estimator existence.

M1.justification: The estimator objective, logistic/binomial/Poisson losses, nonlinear system, and Hilbert-space reformulation are retained. The binomial loss used in v3's added simulations was already defined in v1 Example 2.2.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates synthetic Poisson responses only. v3 additionally evaluates binary and repeated-measurement binomial responses with q = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 (Section 4, Figure 3), materially extending empirical coverage beyond examples previously treated only theoretically.

E2.justification: Both versions compare empirical existence frequencies with the paper's theoretical threshold, without evaluating competing estimators. Added citations and the connection to Candès and Sur do not introduce a separately evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Figure 2 changes the reported Poisson sample size from n = 1000 to 1500, although v3 Section 4 still states 1000; the actual setting remains unresolved. The added binomial experiment specifies n = 1000 and sweeps q and signal strength up to 10, retaining the basic existence-frequency evaluation.

E4.justification: Figure 3 adds a sweep over measurement count q, including an overlay of theoretical threshold curves, examining sensitivity of the existence boundary to repeated measurements. v1's numerical analysis varied dimension ratio and signal strength only for Poisson responses.

E5.justification: Both versions report 20 repetitions per simulation setting and display empirical existence frequencies. The binomial experiments extend this same reporting practice; neither version reports seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v3 adds five binomial phase diagrams and a comparison of threshold curves in Figure 3, showing agreement with predicted existence boundaries and increasing critical p/n with larger q. The Poisson empirical plot also changes, retaining its qualitative agreement with theory; the conflicting sample-size disclosures limit direct comparison.

T1.justification: The principal theorems and formal working assumptions remain. Appendix E.2 corrects the Pythagorean argument from φ(s) ≤ O(s²) to φ(s) ≥ −O(s²) and restores the missing normalization in the constraint. Appendix A.1 also corrects the column-span indexing and ambient dimension. These are local proof repairs.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the stated asymptotic range from δ ∈ (0, ∞) to δ ∈ (1, ∞), matching the restriction already present in v1's introduction. The two central contributions—the general existence threshold and unique solvability precisely above it—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanation of Assumption 2.4 qualifies one-dimensional estimator existence as occurring 'with positive probability'; v1's corresponding discussion asserted existence without that qualification. The differentiability caveat and principal phase-transition interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: v3 documents the added simulation's binomial sampling law, sigmoid success probability, q values, and sample size in Section 4 and Figure 3. The existing Poisson linear-programming description remains, with no additional solver implementation or code-access information.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning through statistical-physics, Gaussian-mixture, random-feature, boosting, and Lasso literature. It credits Montanari et al. with pioneering the Hilbert-space approach and explicitly distinguishes their separable max-margin regime from this paper's complementary M-estimator regime (Sections 1–3).

P1.justification: Section 3 gains an extended explanatory roadmap for both sides of the phase transition, developing ideas previously confined to the appendices. Additional event and Hilbert-space notation explanations, expanded contextual paragraphs, and rewritten proof passages substantially deepen the exposition while retaining the overall section structure.

P2.justification: The single-column manuscript becomes a two-column ICML main text with single-column appendices. Figure 2 moves from the references into Section 2 and is redrawn with revised axes and explicit existence-region labels. v3 also adds the six-panel binomial Figure 3 and revises Figure 1's labeling.

improvement.justification: The added binomial validation, clearer proof roadmap, better research attribution, and local proof corrections provide a modest net improvement in support, clarity, and mathematical accuracy. The central theoretical contribution remains intact. These gains are tempered by v3's unresolved Poisson sample-size discrepancy: Figure 2 states 1500 while Section 4 states 1000.
